speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me understand your condition, can you describe when these episodes started and how long they last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age and the position-dependent nature of your spinning sensation, is there any associated hearing loss, tinnitus, or ear fullness in the affected ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The clinical picture of position-dependent vertigo in a 70-year-old woman without other neurological or auditory deficits strongly suggests canalithiasis in one of the semicircular canals.
